reason: The cited evidence (E1, E3) shows that oxide layers (e.g., ZrTiO4, chromium oxide, high-entropy spinel) improve tribocorrosion and oxidation resistance in HEAs, but none of the passages address the dynamic, cyclic removal-and-regeneration kinetics, the effect of intermittent pauses, or a direct comparison with an oxidation-inhibited baseline. The key premises about the balance of wear and reformation and the predicted outcome are therefore unsupported by the specific prior results cited.
premises: Mechanical sliding removes a pre-existing oxide film on the HEA surface
During pauses in loading, reactive alloy elements rapidly oxidize and regenerate a protective layer
The net degradation rate is determined by the balance between wear-induced film removal and oxidation-driven film reformation
An actively regenerating oxide will reduce combined degradation (wear and corrosion) compared to a baseline where oxidation is inhibited
The proposed mechanism holds at 60 °C in oxygenated aqueous environments but may fail in low-oxygen or overly aggressive conditions
